rounds.proof_sketch: spatial_size = 16*32*32 = 16384; grid_size.x = ceil(16384/256) = 64; max spatial_idx = 64*256-1 = 16383; since 16384 % 256 == 0, no thread ever has spatial_idx == spatial_size, making the >= vs > distinction moot
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-return boundary check from >= to >. However, the fixed input shape produces spatial_size = 16384 after conv_transpose, which is perfectly divisible by the thread block width (256). This means grid_size.x = 64 exactly, and spatial_idx ranges from 0 to 16383. The original predicate (spatial_idx >= 16384) and mutated predicate (spatial_idx > 16384) both evaluate to FALSE for all reachable thread indices [0, 16383]. The boundary case spatial_idx == 16384 where they would differ is never reached.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape contract. The mutation would only be killable if spatial_size were not a multiple of 256, which would require changing the model configuration (kernel_size, stride, padding of conv_transpose) - not allowed under the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should recognize that boundary guard mutations in GPU kernels are often unkillable when grid/block dimensions perfectly tile the problem size. Consider adding static analysis to detect when spatial_size is guaranteed to be a multiple of block_size, marking such boundary mutations as equivalent.
